fields.description:
Which definition of `current_balance` applies to this box.

  • Outstanding — `total_outstanding` (issued + loan given − loan repaid). The right rule for every box except the company's main cash box.
  • Received minus distributed — `total_received` − `total_distributed`. Cash on hand. The right rule for the MAIN cash box.

The default is `Outstanding`, because it is the only default that cannot change a figure somebody already has.
fields.label: Balance Rule

fields.description: Which role this box has for its linked Account's company. Main is declared per company; Custody is the safe default. The company is resolved through cash_account → Account.company.
fields.label: Balance Role
Total Cash
fields.description: The cash that actually moved through this box: received + transfers in - distributed - transfers out. It is computed for EVERY box, whatever `balance_rule` says, because the reconciliation signal is this figure against the GL balance of `cash_account` - and those are different facts (ADR-170). `current_balance` is the rule-selected figure and is not the same thing.

fields.label: Entries
fields.description: ONE ledger. The transfer table is gone: a transfer is an entry whose `other_box` is set, because it moves custody between two boxes, which is a counterparty fact and not a different kind of row (ADR-169).

fields.label: Pending Items
fields.description: What is OWED, one row per obligation. The four `pending_*` columns this replaces held one amount per named person, so adding a fifth person was a schema change; here a party is a row (ADR-169).
